correctness.rationale: For each center-permutive Rule-57 local update, the bit holds exactly for neighbor pair (0,1). In a two-sweep return, any unchanged site forces both neighbors unchanged, hence all unchanged and an impossible fixed point. Thus all sites toggle. Precisely accounting for the old/new neighbor order forces x_(i+2)=1-x_i (0≤i≤n-3) and boundary equalities x_(n-1)=x_1, x_(n-2)=x_0. Solving four residue classes gives exactly four states iff n≡2 mod4, all complementing in two steps. All local site changes are involutive and their composition bijective. Exhaustive implementation n=3..17 and an independent local check n=3..256 corroborate the proof.

value.rationale: Rule 57 is a prominent nonlinear, schedule-sensitive yet center-permutive automaton. The precise minimal nontrivial recurrence sector is a motivated natural invariant: although every fixed-sweep state is periodic, primitive two-cycles exhibit a strict n≡2 mod4 resonance with only two orbits. The hold-propagation dichotomy and two boundary equations provide a reusable structural mechanism explaining this finite population; it is not a textbook substitution or an arbitrary finite enumeration.
